title: Bounded register reachability
statement: Let $P$ be a register program with oracle $	ext{oracle}$, and let $c_0,c_1,c$ be configurations on input $x$, with register $r$ and integer bound $L$. The predicate holds if there is a time $T$ such that running $P$ with the oracle from $c_0$ for $T$ steps gives $c_1$, and for every $t<T$ there are a state $s$, input-head position $ip$, and integer $q$ such that the configuration at time $t$ equals the configuration obtained by replacing the corresponding register data of $c$ by $s,ip,r,q$, the program has no call at $s$, and $-1\le q\le L$.
hypotheses_covered: An oracle from indices in $\{0,\ldots,d-1\}$ and Boolean strings to Booleans
caveat: The supplied statement does not define the run relation or the configuration constructor used in the intermediate-time condition, so their operational meaning is only described structurally.
